newsitem.title: SWEDEN: OLYMPICS-STOCKHOLM TO RALLY SUPPORT IN GAMES BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-STOCKHOLM TO RALLY SUPPORT IN GAMES BID.

text.p: Stockholm Olympic officials pledged to rally public support for the 2004 Summer Games over the next six months after the city was shortlisted on Friday among five bidding to be hosts.

An International Olympic Committee (IOC) evaluation report last month said the Swedish capital had one of the strongest technical bids regarding facilities and organisation but local opposition was seen as hindering its bid.
"The opinion polls have been the biggest disadvantage for Stockholm's bid," said Ulf Adelsohn, a leading campaigner and conservative politican.
Olof Stenhammar of the Stockholm bid committee said Friday's decision would start a new phase of campaigning for the Games which would include rallying public support.
"First thing tomorrow we will start on six months of hard work, internationally as well as continuing the dialogue with the Swedish public," Stenhammar said in a statement.
A poll this week showed a last minute reversal of opinion with more Swedes for than against the bid for the first time.
The poll showed 46 percent in favour of hosting the Olympics -- but 43 percent remained opposed to the bid.
Bjorn Unger, a member of the bid committee, said the change in public opinion was proof of the bid's merits.
"The decision is proof that the executive board has appreciated our ideas for Olympics of a convenient size and with a strong environmental profile," Unger said in a statement.
Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson on Friday welcomed the news that Stockholm was among the finalists, calling it a boost for the country and its athletic programmes.
"I am very glad that Sweden is now among the finalists. Olympic Games in Stockholm in 2004 could be a lift for ... Swedish sports as well as for the entire society," Persson said in a statement.
"I believe Stockholm, with its focus on the environment, its compact size and its enterprising spirit will be very well positioned."
The IOC will vote on Septmeber 5 to decide the 2004 hosts.
